entities.name: Mahabat Khan III of Junagadh
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Sir Muhammad Mahabat Khanji III Rasul Khanji, was the last ruling Nawab of Junagadh of the princely state of Junagadh in India from 1911 to 1948. He was the father of Muhammad Dilawar Khanji – former Governor of Sindh and his claimed successor. Famed for his extravagant lifestyle and his love of dogs, his decision to accede Junagadh to the Dominion of Pakistan following India's Independence led to the Indian Army taking military action. He is credited with pioneering a conservation effort in the Nawab of Junagarh's private hunting grounds, in what is now the Gir National Park, that saved India's last few lions from almost certain extinction.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mahabat Khan III's conservation efforts in the Gir National Park saved India's last few lions from extinction, and his decision to accede Junagadh to Pakistan led to military action by the Indian Army. This event had significant regional implications for the governance of princely states during India's transition to independence.
